review_notes: Read the whole file. The only substantial repetition is in leadingFamily_spans: the "largest support index of a nonzero vector" argument appears twice (inside lower_span and in the final top-level step). The linear independence proof uses max' on a different finset (a Finset of ActiveIndex), so I did not count it. I did not compile the proposed lemma, so its proof is a sketch. Possible rewrite risk: the lemma has to be stated in the file's local-instance LinearOrder ι context. The underlying fact is just support.max' plus mem_support_iff, so I did not look for a Mathlib replacement.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out twice. Take a nonzero vector, show its b.repr is nonzero, take the support, then take max' of the support. Then show every later coordinate vanishes, using le_max', notMem_support_iff and a simpa to turn repr into coord. This is lines 162-172 and 189-194 inside lower_span, and again at lines 227-242 in the final step. The two copies differ only in the vector (z versus x) and in what is done with the index j afterwards. Each copy is about 15 lines, and a change to one has to be mirrored in the other.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma before leadingFamily_spans, stated in the same variables, with the omit for IsDomain and IsPrincipalIdealRing as for the neighbouring lemmas:

private lemma exists_leading_index {x : M} (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ j, b.coord j x ≠ 0 ∧ x ∈ upTo b j

Proof sketch. From hx get b.repr x ≠ 0, using b.repr.injective and map_zero. Take hsupp from Finsupp.support_nonempty_iff, and set j := (b.repr x).support.max' hsupp. Then b.coord j x ≠ 0 comes from max'_mem and mem_support_iff. For x ∈ upTo b j, use mem_upTo_iff: for k > j, k is not in the support, because otherwise le_max' gives k ≤ j. Then notMem_support_iff gives b.coord k x = 0.

Use 1, in lower_span, after by_cases hz0, obtain ⟨j, hjc, hjup⟩ := exists_leading_index b (z := (z : M)) hzval. Then j ≤ i by_contra: if i < j, then (mem_upTo_iff b).mp hz_up j gives b.coord j z = 0, contradicting hjc. Next j ≠ i, since b.coord i z = 0 by hz_coord. So j < i, and the step finishes with exact ih j hji z hjup.

Use 2, at the end, obtain ⟨j, -, hjup⟩ := exists_leading_index b hxval and finish with exact h_upTo j x hjup.

The two hxval/hzval conversions from z ≠ 0 in N to (z : M) ≠ 0 can stay as they are.
findings.benefit: The max-support argument is proved once and named. lower_span shrinks to the ordering argument (j ≤ i and j ≠ i), and the final step becomes two lines. The nontrivial finite-support reasoning is stated as a single reusable fact, so a reader no longer has to check that the two copies agree.
